 The biggest video game release of the decade has been extra exciting for a handful of Canadian actors, who, after years of secrecy, can finally discuss their latest gig.
 Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest in Rockstar Games’ beloved Grand Theft Auto franchise, has already received high praise for its detailed world-building – the title is currently the highest-scoring video game of all time on Metacritic, boasting a score of 99 out of 100. In addition to its lifelike terrains and cars, the game’s fictionalized version of Miami features 30,000 unique NPCs, or non-playable characters, who populate virtual depictions of the city’s streets, clubs and beaches.
 Grand Theft Auto VI has fans calling in sick and singing its praises 
 Alex Kelly, Preston Vendramin, Nicola Hadjis and Macayla Paris are among the hundreds of actors who contributed to the motion capture process behind Grand Theft Auto VI ’s thousands of NPCs, as well as the game’s lead characters. Prior to GTA VI , none of these performers had worked with the technology, which uses special suits to track performers’ movements, generating data that can then be used to create realistic animations. 
 Macayla Paris
 Supplied
 Alex Kelly
 Supplied
 But the four actors share a background in live theatre. Kelly, for instance, is going into his fourth season at the Stratford Festival. Vendramin appeared in Harold Green Jewish Theatre’s recent Yiddish production of Fiddler on the Roof ; Hadjis and Paris have performed in musicals in Toronto and beyond.
 “As an actor and a dancer, you’re very in tune with your body,” said Vendramin. “I think that lends itself really well to this sort of work. The nature of motion capture is very physical.” His colleagues concurred: Theatre acting, they said, provides actors with a finely tuned sense of bodily awareness that makes the micromovements of motion capture easier to achieve in fewer takes.
 GTA VI and the death of the disc 
 “You’re very meticulous about where your foot is placed, or how you’re moving,” said Kelly. “Knowing how your own body works was so beneficial for this kind of job.”
 Open this photo in gallery: Preston Vendramin Preston Vendramin/Supplied 
 Vendramin, citing Rockstar’s famously strict non-disclosure agreements, declined to provide specifics of what GTA VI ’s motion capture process entailed. But, broadly speaking, actors worked with session directors to capture “certain physical attributes,” following instructions to walk or move their limbs in a certain way. (Preston hinted that his special skills in areas such as stage combat and marksmanship came in handy.)
 Keeping the secret was harder for some actors than others. Vendramin is a devotee of the Grand Theft Auto series: During the pandemic, he completed GTA V on his PlayStation 4, in addition to winning all of the available trophies within the notoriously time-consuming game. While Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, never confirmed to the actors what they were working on – “They were very tight-lipped on what this was,” said Vendramin – as time went on, the performer had a feeling he was about to be a part of history.
 Open this photo in gallery: Nicola Hadjis Nicola Hadjis/Supplied 
 Hadjis, also a frequent gamer, agreed: “It was one of the hardest secrets to keep,” she said. “This is obviously something you want to shout from the rooftops.” A few actors listed their work as “untitled motion-capture project” on their CVs – “so at least it looked like I was accomplishing something with my life over the last four years,” joked Hadjis. When eagle-eyed GTA fans connected the dots between the vague CV credits and the coming game, the performers were floored.
 “I don’t know if the FBI is looking for recruits, but I think there’s some potential there,” continued Hadjis with a laugh. “People were doing some serious sleuthing.”
 Paris, meanwhile, isn’t much of a video game enthusiast – her experience with the pastime is mostly limited to Mario Kart. But the challenge of applying her background in dance to the new world of motion capture was rewarding, she said, even without an existing affinity for the project at hand.
 “As an actor, sometimes we forget our face is doing a lot of the work for us,” she said. “With motion capture, you don’t have that to rely on. Focusing your body and making it expressive to tell the story clearly was a really cool turning point for me. I learned a lot as an actor.”
 “This was a once-in-a-lifetime experience,” said Vendramin. “I mean, this is probably one of the greatest gaming companies in the world. There is only going to be one GTA VI release. It’s an amazing feeling to be immortalized in something this great.”
